figmaExecutionNotes: Use a single dark-theme page system rather than alternating light/dark patterns unless needed for readability.
Keep trust logos visually dominant; badges support but should not replace the logo strip.
Follow design-system-first spacing: section padding 80px desktop, consistent 24px container gutters.
For mobile, stack hero with media above text, convert all feature grids to single column, and keep gallery as a swipeable vertical stack or one-column carousel treatment.
Do not add unsupported sections such as pricing, testimonials, forms, or news because they are not present in the input.
Preserve copy verbatim for headlines, subheadlines, and feature titles/descriptions where provided.

heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro — advanced foundation models for professional image and video creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a premium dark editorial hero with a layered center composition: a large headline block on the left, an offset media stack on the right, and floating orange-accent proof chips around a framed product preview. The hero should feel cinematic but B2B-trustworthy, with subtle grid lines, soft spotlighting, and orange CTA emphasis. The main visual should be a composed UI/mockup shell rather than a generic lifestyle image, while the secondary visual acts as a preview card for Seedance video output. Keep the layout unexpected by using a dominant background-overlay composition instead of a standard split layout, and reserve motion for subtle staggered entrance and hover lift only.

repetitionBreakers: Start with a content-first hero, then switch immediately into a logo-heavy trust band to satisfy warm traffic continuity without repeating the hero layout.
Use alternating light/dark section backgrounds so consecutive blocks never feel visually static.
Present Seedream and Seedance as two distinct product experiences: the first with a visual preview-led spotlight, the second with a split-panel comparison and motion emphasis.
Use a carousel for testimonials instead of a static grid because there are 5 testimonials.
Keep CTA placement conversion-led but restrained: one dominant hero CTA, one proof-adjacent CTA, and a final pricing CTA, all labeled exactly 'Get started'.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Create professional AI images and videos with ByteDance models Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Explore high-quality generation, synchronized audio-video, and enterprise-ready creative workflows.

sections.backgroundTreatment: dark editorial field with precision-line accents, floating pill chips, and subtle glow emphasis around the CTA
sections.designNote: Content-first hero that answers what this is, who it is for, and what to do next. Keep the headline direct and premium, preserve the current ad message for continuity, and make the CTA the brightest object on the page. Use the existing headline and subheadline structure, but visually compress the long copy into a tight, high-contrast editorial stack. Add a short supporting line beneath the CTA that reinforces text-to-image, image editing, and text-to-video workflows.

Immediate trust reset after the hero: a prominent logo strip using 3-6 recognizable partner logos if available, otherwise fallback to a metric strip. Keep it wide, motion-light, and enterprise-coded. This section should feel like a credibility band rather than a decorative footer.

Three-step process section under 60 seconds, designed as a quick vertical narrative with alternating micro-visuals beside each step. Step 1: enter prompt or upload reference. Step 2: refine image/video direction. Step 3: generate and export professional output. Use compact cards with strong numbering and one-line explanations. This section should feel fast, practical, and visually different from the hero and trust band.

Proof section stays industry-facing and logo-led. If the provided logos are insufficient, substitute a metric strip. Include a short credibility headline and keep the visual rhythm compact. This block should sit before deep feature exploration because warm traffic expects proof after the quick workflow explanation.

Use alternating product blocks rather than a generic SaaS grid. First product block: Seedream 4.5 in a visual-first split panel with a preview area and capability list focused on the 1-2 features that drove the click: high-resolution generation and multimodal editing. Second product block: Seedance 1.5 Pro in a motion-led split panel with audio-video synchronization and cinematic camera control emphasized. Avoid flat cards for the 5+ feature lists; convert each into a spotlight-plus-list treatment or a compact accordion with a live preview panel. Keep adjacency contrast strong: light-to-dark, editorial-to-technical.

Expressive showcase section with video thumbnails and cinematic motion stills. This is one of the two most visually expressive sections on the page. Use a dominant preview on one side and a tight supporting strip of output examples on the other. Keep it premium, image-led, and clearly distinct from the product explainer blocks.

Inquiry-oriented pricing presented as two focused cards, not a noisy pricing table. Highlight the Seedance option slightly if the buyer is video-led, but keep both visible. The CTA must remain exactly 'Get started' and should be solid accent orange, full-width on mobile, and never gray or outlined. This section should read as the conversion bridge.

Use a carousel because there are 5 testimonials. Structure quotes around professional outcomes: turnaround time, synchronized audio-video storytelling, and precision editing. Include author role and company if available. Keep the carousel restrained and editorial, not bubbly.

Final CTA section with a centered form card and a strong closing prompt. Keep it minimal and decisive. The button text must be exactly 'Get started'. This is the last conversion step, so visually simplify and remove unnecessary distractions.

Utility-style footer band with logos or media marks only if useful; otherwise keep it minimal. It should not compete with the final CTA. Use as a low-key credibility echo rather than a content-heavy footer.

blueprint.designPersonality: Confident, creative, and enterprise-ready: a dark editorial AI showcase anchored by trust logos, precise typography, and cinematic video gallery moments, with orange brand accents used sparingly for emphasis and conversion.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a premium editorial visual system: dark hero with floating proof chips, a dominant marquee logo band, and a gallery section featuring embedded video thumbnails and cinematic motion stills. Product visuals should feel like an AI creative suite dashboard rendered as polished PNG shells, with subtle orange highlights, crisp typography overlays, and layered composition previews.

mustHaveMoments: Above-the-fold logo wall or recognizable brand/trust strip placed before deeper persuasion content

avoidPatterns: Overly decorative or cluttered AI-themed visuals that reduce credibility

Deep tabbed navigation that hides key product capabilities

designStrategy.reasoning: This page should function as a high-intent lead-generation asset for professionals evaluating advanced generative AI tools. The audience is solution-aware and needs confidence, clarity, and proof rather than education from scratch. Because the visitor trusts logos most, the design should lead with recognizable trust signals and then quickly move into product value. A dark theme will help position the product as modern and premium while making generated visuals and video gallery content stand out. The narrative should remain product-led, with a split hero that communicates both Seedream and Seedance clearly, followed by structured sections that explain capabilities in a scannable way. Since the goal is inquiry and demo generation, CTA pressure should be medium: prominent and repeated, but not aggressive. A gallery section containing video examples is essential because motion output is the strongest proof for Seedance, while testimonials and pricing/quote blocks close the loop for decision-makers.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
